random-section.title: Effects included in the randomized sets:

about-text.description: Disintegrate your windows with style. Version: ext-version Ported to Cinnamon by Kevin Langman Github / Report an issue / Website Based on the Burn-My-Windows code by Schneegans and contributors Github / Ko-fi The Magic Lamp Effect is ported from code by hermes83 Github

app-rules.tooltip: A list of applications with special effect rules. The application can be a desktop file name or a WM_CLASS name

app-rules-button.description: Add entry for the application of the most recently focused window
app-rules-button.tooltip: Focus a window you want to enable application specific setting for then return here and press this button.

random-include.description: Effects included in the randomized sets
random-include.tooltip: Defines which effects are included in the randomized sets for each window event type. When 'Randomized' is selected for any event on the General tab these sets are used.

enable-sound.description: Allow Burn My Windows to override cinnamon sound effects
enable-sound.tooltip: Allow Burn My Windows to override Cinnamon's window open/close/minimize sound effects with unique ones defined in the Effect Settings tab for each Burn My Windows effect. Note: Sounds will only play when Cinnamon's open/close/minimize sound effects are enabled under Cinnamon sounds settings. The default cinnamon sounds will be used unless a sound effect file is chosen for the active Burn My Windows effect.

dialog-special.tooltip: Allows you to define special settings for handling dialog window types (i.e. file open dialog windows). These settings will override any application specific settings that may have been defined.

power-dialog-special.tooltip: Allows you to define special settings for handling dialog window types (i.e. file open dialog windows).

power-onbattery.description: Use different effects when running on battery power
power-onbattery.tooltip: When enabled, a set of options will appear allowing you to define which effects (if any) will be used when running on battery power and the battery charge state is less than the set limit. These settings will take precedence over both the general settings and any application specific settings when the battery charge state condition is met.

aperture-panels-panel-size.tooltip: The approximate size of the panels. It is adjusted a little so that a whole number of panels fits the window exactly.

aperture-panels-wave-shape.tooltip: The shape of the wave of panels flipping across the window. Random picks one of the shapes for each animation.

aperture-panels-flip-axis.tooltip: The axis the panels turn around. Random picks one for each animation.

aperture-panels-backdrop.tooltip: What is seen behind the panels as they turn. Wallpaper: the desktop stays in place and only the windows behind are on the panels. Black void: the desktop is on the panels too and flips with them, revealing a black void.

aperture-panels-border-style.tooltip: When the outlines of the panels are shown: only while a panel flips, or also in a band ahead of and/or behind the wave of flipping panels.

fire-3d-noise.tooltip: Creates a more dynamic fire but requires more GPU power.

fire-random-color.description: Use a Random Color (overrides other color settings)
fire-random-color.tooltip: Use a random fire color. This setting will override any preset or custom colors settings you select.

focus-blur-quality.tooltip: The Quality of the Blur (Setting this too high may increase GPU load and affect performance)

hexagon-additive-blending.tooltip: You may want to enable this for dark window themes.

incinerate-use-pointer.tooltip: If disabled, a random location will be chosen.

magiclamp-effect.tooltip: The effect can be a smooth curve or a wavy animation. The random option will randomly choose between the two and the Appear/Disappear options use different effects whether a window is appearing or disappearing from the screen

magiclamp-edge.tooltip: The monitor edge where a window should originate from when opening, or disappear towards when closing. This setting is not used for minimize or unminimize events

magiclamp-edge-offset.tooltip: The offset from the top or left of the "Open/Close Edge" that the animation should use as the origin/target of the animation. This is a percentage of the monitors width/height and it does not apply to minimize/unminimize events or when the "Open/Close Edge" is set to "Edge closest to mouse pointer"

magiclamp-x-tiles.tooltip: This effects the quality and the cost of the animation

magiclamp-y-tiles.tooltip: This effects the quality and the costs of the animation

morph-style.tooltip: Liquid flow: the area swirls into the window like liquid. Melt: each image flows along its own edges, so what's behind melts away and the window's outlines form first.

morph-strength.tooltip: How far things move during the morph. 1 is the default; 0 is a plain dissolve.

wormhole-bounce.tooltip: How much the desktop bounces when the effect lands (0 = no bounce)

test-effect.tooltip: Opens a window using the currently selected effect.
